areas.area_name: Mine (open-cut gibbsitic bauxite: clearing, stripping, drill & blast, load & haul, ROM pad, primary sizing, grade control, dewatering, rehabilitation)
areas.purpose: Deliver ~6.2-6.4 Mt/yr wet run-of-mine (ROM) gibbsitic bauxite of controlled quality (available Al2O3, reactive SiO2) to the mine primary sizing station and overland conveyor, while progressively rehabilitating mined land. Plateau-type lateritic bauxite deposit (India East Coast Khondalite-plateau style; Darling Range-style noted where different): thin overburden, hard ferricrete/duricrust caprock, friable to clayey bauxite ore horizon over kaolinitic clay floor.
areas.process_description: 1) Planning & grade control: exploration drilling (~60-120 m grid) defines ore pods; infill/grade-control drilling (RC or aircore, ~7.5-15 m grid, 0.5-1.0 m sample intervals) is assayed by XRF plus a laboratory low-temperature (approx. 143-150 degC) caustic micro-digestion to report AVAILABLE Al2O3 (gibbsite alumina) and REACTIVE SiO2 (kaolinite silica that forms desilication product in the refinery). Ore/waste and grade-bin polygons are loaded into excavator high-precision GPS guidance and the fleet management system (FMS). 2) Clearing: vegetation and merchantable timber are removed by dozers (timber salvage, mulch retained for rehab). 3) Topsoil stripping: the top ~0.1-0.3 m (seed bank) is stripped separately by dozer push/wheel loader and either directly returned to an area being rehabilitated or stockpiled (low, <2 m high) for reuse. 4) Overburden removal: ~0.3-2 m of soil/laterite overburden is dozed or excavated and hauled to backfill mined-out pits (low strip ratio, typically 0.3-0.6 t waste per t ore; engineering estimate). 5) Caprock drill & blast: the hard cemented ferricrete/duricrust (0.5-3 m thick; UCS roughly 20-80 MPa, engineering estimate) is drilled (89-127 mm holes) and blasted with bulk emulsion/ANFO on shallow benches; where its available alumina is adequate it is mined AS ORE (common in the Darling Range), otherwise as waste. Soft bauxite below is free-dug or ripped. 6) Load & haul: 200-t-class hydraulic backhoe excavators (and a large wheel loader for flexibility) load ~90-t-class rear-dump trucks; trucks haul 2-8 km on engineered haul roads either directly to the dump hopper of the primary sizing station or to ROM-pad grade-bin fingers. The FMS assigns trucks to sources so that the delivered ore meets blend targets (e.g. reactive SiO2 below an agreed ceiling, available Al2O3 above a floor). 7) Primary sizing: trucks dump into a 2-sided hopper; an apron feeder draws ore into a twin-shaft primary sizer that reduces ROM (up to ~1.2-1.5 m) to -200 mm, suitable for the 1,200 mm overland belt. Oversize/locked boulders are broken by a pedestal rock breaker. A metal detector and self-cleaning magnet protect the overland belt from tramp steel (bucket teeth, drill steel). 8) Dewatering & water management: pits on plateau tops are mostly rainfall-fed; diesel dry-prime pumps lift sump water to sediment ponds; clean-water diversion drains route runoff around pits; haul roads are watered for dust control. 9) Rehabilitation: pit floor shaped to final landform; overburden then topsoil returned; deep ripping on the contour (to ~1.0-2.0 m) with winged tines to break the compacted floor; seeding/planting with local species; monitoring to completion criteria. Typical sequence clearing-to-rehab is 1-3 years per pit (Alcoa Darling Range practice, Koch 2007). NOTE high-temperature/boehmitic deposits (e.g. Weipa-type, Guinea) are mined similarly; differences are in the refinery, not the mine. Darling Range ore is lower grade (approx. 27-33% available Al2O3, high quartz) giving larger tonnages per t alumina.

streams.name: ROM bauxite (ore) to primary sizer / ROM pad
streams.from_to: Pits (01-EX/01-FL loading 01-HT trucks) -> 01-HP-001 dump hopper / 01-RP-001 ROM pad
streams.flow: ~6.2-6.4 Mt/yr wet; ~1,300-1,500 t/h average while crushing (~4,300-4,900 effective crushing h/yr); peak tipping rate up to ~2,000-2,400 t/h
streams.composition: Design ore: total Al2O3 45-48%, available Al2O3 ~40% (range 38-43%), reactive SiO2 1.5-2.5% (blend ceiling ~2.5%), total SiO2 2-5%, Fe2O3 18-25%, TiO2 1.5-3%, LOI ~24-26%; free moisture 8-12% (higher in monsoon). Lump size up to ~1.2-1.5 m
streams.basis: Engineering estimate from 2.0 Mt/yr alumina x bauxite factor 2.7 t dry/t plus ~3-5% dilution/ore loss and 10% moisture; India East Coast-type grade per published descriptions (Authier-Martin et al. 2001, Hudson et al. Ullmann's)

streams.name: Overburden and waste caprock
streams.from_to: Pits -> backfill of mined-out pits / temporary waste dumps
streams.composition: Lateritic soil, low-grade ferricrete, kaolinitic clay

streams.name: Topsoil
streams.from_to: Cleared areas -> direct return to rehab areas or topsoil stockpiles
streams.composition: Organic-rich surface soil with seed bank; handled when dry-moist, never when saturated

streams.name: Sized ore to overland system
streams.basis: Engineering estimate consistent with 1,200 mm belt (CEMA lump guidance)

streams.name: Pit dewatering water
streams.from_to: Pit sumps -> 01-PP-001/002 -> 01-SP-001 sediment ponds -> reuse for dust suppression / controlled discharge
streams.flow: Highly seasonal; design ~150-300 L/s per active pit group in monsoon storms
streams.composition: Rainwater with suspended clay/bauxite fines (TSS can exceed 1,000 mg/L before settling)
streams.basis: Engineering estimate; size to site design storm (e.g. 1-in-10 yr 72 h)

streams.name: Haul road dust-suppression water
streams.from_to: Sediment ponds / raw-water standpipes -> 01-WC water carts -> haul roads
streams.basis: Engineering estimate (approx. 1-2 L/m2 per application, several passes/shift)

equipment.name: Grade-control drill rig (RC / aircore) with sample splitter
equipment.function: Drills closely spaced grade-control holes ahead of mining and recovers representative interval samples for available Al2O3 / reactive SiO2 / Fe2O3 assays used to define ore boundaries and grade bins.
equipment.type_selected: Track- or truck-mounted reverse-circulation (RC) / aircore rig with on-board compressor, cyclone and rotary cone splitter
equipment.why_this_type: Dry chip samples with low contamination at 0.5-1 m resolution; fast in soft lateritic profiles; aircore suits soft clay-rich bauxite, RC needed through hard caprock.
equipment.alternatives: Diamond core (exploration/QAQC only, slow); auger (cheap but contamination/smearing); FTIR/DRIFTS on drill powders for rapid available alumina/reactive silica estimation (used as screening).
key_dimensions: Rig footprint ~10-12 m long x 2.5-3 m wide, mast ~8-10 m high when raised (engineering estimate)
Hole diameter ~85-140 mm; depth typically 5-30 m (through bauxite to clay floor)
Drill grid ~7.5-15 m (grade control) vs 60-120 m (exploration) (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: Available Al2O3 & reactive SiO2 (low-temp micro-digestion ~143-150 degC), XRF total oxides, LOI

equipment.working_principle: Compressed air drives a down-the-hole hammer or blade bit while a dual-wall rod string returns cuttings up the inner tube (reverse circulation), so chips from the bit face are not mixed with wall material. Cuttings pass through a cyclone that drops the solids into a rotary cone splitter, which divides each interval into a laboratory sub-sample (~2-5 kg) and a reject. Sample bags are numbered by hole and depth. In the laboratory the samples are dried, crushed, pulverised and digested in caustic at low temperature to replicate refinery digestion, giving available alumina and reactive silica, the two numbers that drive refinery economics. Results feed a block model that defines ore polygons and grade bins.
details_to_model: Crawler or 6x6 truck carrier with folding mast (lattice or box section), rod carousel holding ~6 m dual-wall rods
Top-drive rotation head running on mast rails; dust hood at collar
Cyclone (~0.6 m dia) on a frame beside the mast, with flexible sample hose from rod head
Rotary cone splitter beneath cyclone with numbered calico/plastic sample bags on a rack, reject pile rows on ground in grid
Auxiliary booster compressor trailer; water tank for dust suppression
Collar marked by survey peg/flag; grid of drilled holes with sample piles in rows
Operator cabin or control panel with emergency stop, guarding around rotating rods (rod-handler cage)
hazards_and_safety: Rotating rods and rod handling (entanglement, pinch points) - guarding, interlocked rod handler
High-pressure air hoses - whip checks on all couplings
Respirable dust incl. crystalline silica - dust hood, water injection, P2 respirators
Working on uncleared ground - snakes/wildlife, uneven ground, rig rollover on slopes
Noise >100 dB(A) - hearing protection
sources: Authier-Martin M., Forte G., Ostap S., See J. (2001) The mineralogy of bauxite for producing smelter-grade alumina, JOM 53(12):36-40
Donoghue A.M., Frisch N., Olney D. (2014) Bauxite mining and alumina refining: process description and occupational health risks, J Occup Environ Med 56(5S):S12-S17
ISO 8685 Aluminium ores - Sampling procedures; ISO 6140 Aluminium ores - Preparation of samples
operating_tips_and_key_points: Reactive silica, not total silica, drives caustic soda and alumina loss (DSP); grade control must report it.
Twin field duplicates and certified reference materials (QAQC) at ~1 in 20 samples.
Do not drill wet clay in heavy rain - smearing and sample bias.

equipment.name: Track-type tractors (dozers) with single-shank ripper
equipment.function: Vegetation clearing, topsoil and overburden stripping, ripping soft caprock/ore, pit floor and dump shaping, deep contour ripping during rehabilitation, haul-road and ROM-pad maintenance.
equipment.type_selected: ~70-t class crawler dozer (e.g. Caterpillar D10 / Komatsu D375A class), semi-U blade, single-shank parallelogram ripper; one unit fitted with rehabilitation winged-tine ripper
equipment.why_this_type: Bauxite profile is thin and laterally extensive, so stripping and ripping are dozer-intensive; D10 class gives ripping force for ferricrete while remaining mobile between scattered pits.
equipment.alternatives: D11 class (higher ripping productivity, less mobile); wheel tractor scrapers for topsoil; surface miners for ripping-free selective mining.
key_dimensions: Length with blade and ripper ~9-10 m, width over blade ~5.0-5.3 m, height to cab ROPS ~4.0-4.2 m (Caterpillar/Komatsu spec, approximate)
Operating mass ~65-72 t
Semi-U blade capacity ~18-20 m3; ripper max penetration ~1.5-2.0 m

operating_parameters.basis: Koch (2007) Alcoa practice (deep ripping); engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: A diesel engine drives the tracks through a torque converter / powershift (or electric drive) and a high-sprocket final drive. Hydraulic cylinders control blade lift, tilt and pitch; the operator pushes material in slots to minimise spillage. The rear ripper shank is hydraulically forced into the ground and pulled forward, fracturing caprock or compacted floors along the shank path so material can be dozed or loaded. In rehabilitation, winged tines lift and shatter the compacted pit floor on the contour so water infiltrates and roots can penetrate. Machine guidance (GNSS) shows the operator design surfaces and ore/topsoil boundaries.
details_to_model: Elevated (high-drive) sprocket, track frames with ~7-8 bottom rollers, grouser shoes ~610-710 mm
Semi-U blade with replaceable cutting edges and end bits, push-arms and tilt cylinder
Single-shank ripper with replaceable tip and shank protector, parallelogram linkage, 2 lift cylinders
ROPS/FOPS cab with access ladder and handrails on left, GNSS antenna masts on cab roof, rotating beacon, LED work lights
Fire suppression nozzles in engine bay, fuel fill point with ground-level access, radiator guard
Rehab unit: three winged tines (rear) instead of single shank
hazards_and_safety: Rollover on slopes and pit edges - ROPS, seatbelt interlocks, edge bunds
Interaction with light vehicles - positive communication, proximity detection / collision avoidance
Ripper shank and blade crushing during maintenance - lower attachments to ground, LOTO
Hot engine surfaces and fuel - fire suppression system
Whole-body vibration and noise
sources: Caterpillar Performance Handbook (Ed. 49/50) - D10 track-type tractor data
Koch J.M. (2007) Alcoa's mining and restoration process in south western Australia, Restoration Ecology 15(4 Suppl):S11-S16
operating_tips_and_key_points: Strip topsoil only when moisture is suitable to protect seed bank; keep topsoil and overburden separate.
Rip on the contour in rehab to reduce erosion.

equipment.name: Crawler blast-hole drill rigs
equipment.function: Drill blast holes in hard ferricrete/duricrust caprock (and occasional hard ore lenses) for fragmentation before loading.
equipment.type_selected: Self-propelled crawler surface drill rig, top-hammer or DTH, 89-127 mm holes, with on-board compressor, rod changer and dust collector (e.g. Sandvik DP/DI series, Epiroc SmartROC D series class)
equipment.why_this_type: Caprock benches are shallow (1-4 m) and widely dispersed; small-diameter rigs give good fragmentation control, low vibration and fast tramming between pits.
equipment.alternatives: Ripping with D10/D11 dozers where caprock UCS is low; surface miners (cut instead of blast); large rotary drills (unsuitable for shallow benches).
key_dimensions: Rig ~11-13 m long (boom stowed), ~2.5 m wide, mast ~9-10 m (engineering estimate from OEM class)
Mass ~18-25 t
Hole dia 89-127 mm, depth 1.5-5 m, pattern ~3.0 x 3.5 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A diesel engine powers hydraulic pumps (tramming, feed, rotation) and a screw compressor. In top-hammer mode a hydraulic percussion drifter on the feed beam strikes the drill string while rotating it; in DTH mode the hammer sits behind the bit at the bottom of the hole. Compressed air flushes cuttings out of the hole, where a collar hood and dust collector with cartridge filters capture the dust. Holes are drilled to pattern using GNSS hole navigation, then dipped and logged before charging with bulk emulsion or ANFO by a mobile manufacturing unit, primed with boosters and electronic detonators, stemmed and fired after the area is cleared.
details_to_model: Crawler undercarriage with oscillating track frames, cab (ROPS/FOPS) with large front window
Boom and feed beam (aluminium or steel) with drifter/rotation head, centraliser, rod carousel (5-8 rods)
Dust hood at hole collar connected by flexible hose to dry dust collector (cartridge filters) on the rig deck
Compressor and engine compartment with side doors, exhaust stack
GNSS antennas on cab/feed, rotating beacon, work lights
Field model: grid of holes with collar markers, stemming piles, blast exclusion signage
hazards_and_safety: Explosives: misfires, flyrock, premature initiation - AS 2187.2 / DGMS rules, blast exclusion zone (typ. >= 300-500 m for personnel; site-specific)
Drilling into misfired holes - never drill into or near old sockets
Silica dust - wet or dry collection, cab filtration
Rig instability on bench edges
sources: AS 2187.2-2006 Explosives - Storage and use - Use of explosives
Sandvik / Epiroc surface drill rig product literature (class data)
common_problems: Hole collapse in clay-rich zones - use casing/stemming plugs
Water in holes in monsoon - use emulsion not ANFO

equipment.name: Hydraulic backhoe excavators (primary loading units)
equipment.function: Selective loading of ore (and caprock/overburden) into haul trucks, following ore/waste boundaries using high-precision GNSS bucket guidance.
equipment.type_selected: ~200-t class diesel-hydraulic backhoe excavator (e.g. Komatsu PC2000, Liebherr R 9200, Hitachi EX1900 class), backhoe bucket ~10-12.5 m3
equipment.why_this_type: Backhoe configuration digs from the top of thin seams down to the clay floor, giving selective control of the ore-floor contact (minimising clay dilution and reactive silica). Matched to 90-t trucks in ~5-6 passes.
equipment.alternatives: Face shovel (better for high faces, less selective at floor); front-end loaders (mobile, less selective); surface miners.
key_dimensions: Operating mass ~190-210 t; tail swing radius ~6 m; overall width ~5.5-6 m (OEM class, approx.)
Max dig depth ~8-9 m, max dump height ~7.5-8 m (OEM class, approx.)
Bucket 10-12.5 m3 with 5-6 GET teeth

operating_parameters.unit: t per pass (loose density ~1.4-1.5 t/m3, fill factor 0.9)

equipment.working_principle: A diesel engine drives variable-displacement hydraulic pumps; control valves direct oil to the boom, stick and bucket cylinders, the swing motors and the travel motors. The operator curls the bucket through the face, swings the upper structure through ~60-90 degrees and dumps into the truck body. Bucket-tip GNSS guidance displays the ore polygon boundaries and the design floor so the operator stops at the clay contact, which is critical because the floor clay is high in reactive silica. Each bucket is weighed by a payload system so truck loads are consistent.
details_to_model: Crawler undercarriage with 2 travel motors, ~6-7 bottom rollers per side, triple grouser shoes ~800 mm
Upper structure: counterweight, engine house with large radiator/cooler, hydraulic tank, fuel tank (~3,000-3,500 L)
Elevated cab with walkways, handrails and a hydraulically lowered access stairway (EMESRT style)
Boom, stick, 2 boom cylinders, 1 stick cylinder, 1 bucket cylinder with hoses routed along boom
Backhoe bucket with lip shroud, 5-6 teeth/adapters, wing shrouds, wear plates
Central auto-lube system, fire suppression, GNSS antennas on counterweight, LED lights, rotating beacon, camera on counterweight
hazards_and_safety: Swing radius crush zone - exclusion zone barricading; no personnel on ground within reach
Trucks being loaded - operator stays in cab; never load over cab
Undercutting high walls/caprock faces - face height limits
Hydraulic oil injection injuries and hose bursts - hose shields, depressurise before maintenance
Working at height on upper deck - handrails, harness points
sources: Caterpillar Performance Handbook (cycle times, fill factors)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Dig the floor last and clean, keep 0.1-0.3 m above clay contact if grade control says so
Present truck at optimum swing angle (~45-70 deg) and double-side load where possible

equipment.name: Large wheel loaders
equipment.function: Flexible loading at small/remote pods, ROM-pad blending rehandle into the dump hopper, cleanup, stockpile management.
equipment.type_selected: ~95-100 t class wheel loader (e.g. Caterpillar 992 class / Komatsu WA900 class), rock bucket ~10-12 m3
equipment.why_this_type: High mobility between dispersed pits and the ROM pad; can blend grade-bin stockpiles directly into the hopper.
equipment.alternatives: Additional excavator (less mobile); integrated tool carriers for small tasks.
key_dimensions: Length ~15-16 m, width over bucket ~5.5 m, height to cab ~6 m (OEM class, approx.)
Tyres 45/65R45 class (~3 m diameter)
equipment.working_principle: Articulated-frame loader: diesel engine, torque converter and planetary powershift drive all four wheels; Z-bar linkage lifts and crowds the bucket. The machine charges the pile, crowds, reverses and turns to load the truck or hopper. On the ROM pad it takes bucketloads from different grade-bin fingers in a set ratio to make a blended feed.
details_to_model: Articulated frame with centre hinge, large rock bucket with segment edges
Cab with front access stairs, platform handrails, rear-view cameras
Rock tyres with tyre chains option, mud guards
Payload weighing display, beacon, lights, fire suppression
hazards_and_safety: Articulation pinch point - frame lock during maintenance
Reversing - cameras, radar, proximity detection
Tyre explosion/handling - tyre exclusion zones, nitrogen inflation

equipment.name: Rear-dump haul trucks (~90-t class)
equipment.function: Haul ore to the primary sizer dump hopper or ROM pad, and overburden/waste caprock to backfill.
equipment.type_selected: Mechanical-drive rigid rear-dump truck, ~90-98 t payload (e.g. Caterpillar 777 / Komatsu HD785 class)
equipment.why_this_type: Bauxite pits are shallow and dispersed with moderate haul distances (2-8 km) and the deposit requires selective mining; 90-t trucks match 200-t excavators, keep haul-road width/construction cost moderate and give fleet granularity. Fleet sizing: cycle ~27 min (load 3.5, haul 5 km loaded ~12, dump 1.5, return ~8.5, spot/queue 1.5) -> ~200 t/h nominal, ~165 t/h effective; ~6,000 effective h/yr -> ~1.0 Mt/yr per truck; 6.3 Mt ore -> ~6-7 trucks + 2 on waste -> 9 operating + 2 spare (engineering estimate).
equipment.alternatives: 136-t (CAT 785 class) or 180-t trucks for longer, wider hauls (fewer operators); road trains/side-tippers on public-road-quality haul roads for long hauls; trolley-assist or battery-electric trucks for decarbonisation.
key_dimensions: Length ~10.5 m, width ~6.1-6.5 m, height (body down) ~5.0-5.2 m, height body raised ~10 m (OEM class, approx.)
Tyres 27.00R49 (diameter ~2.7 m) -> windrow/berm height >= ~1.4 m
Body heaped capacity ~60-65 m3 (bauxite liner, tailgate optional)

operating_parameters.basis: OEM rimpull curves (approx.); site speed limits apply

equipment.working_principle: A V-12 diesel drives the rear axle through a torque converter, automatic planetary powershift transmission, differential and planetary final drives. Oil-cooled multi-disc brakes and engine/retarder braking control speed on downgrades, which is critical on plateau-to-valley haul roads. At the dump the body is raised by two multi-stage hoist cylinders; material slides out over the tail. Payload monitoring (strut-pressure based) and the FMS log every load (source, destination, tonnage) to reconcile ore quality to the refinery.
details_to_model: Rigid frame, 2 axles, 6 tyres (dual rear), front suspension struts
Dual-slope or flat-floor dump body with canopy (cab protector), body liner plates, rock ejectors between rear duals
Two body hoist cylinders, body pivot pins at rear of frame
Left-side cab with diagonal stairway access across radiator front, platform handrails, ROPS/FOPS
Large front radiator grille, exhaust routed through body (body heating) or vertical stack
Fire suppression bottles, auto-lube, mud flaps, number plates (large fleet numbers on body and cab), beacons, buggy whip flag, rear cameras, proximity radar, GNSS/FMS antenna
Model loaded/empty states, body raised position at hopper
hazards_and_safety: Collisions with light vehicles (blind spots up to ~10+ m) - segregation, buggy whips, CAS/proximity detection, positive radio communication
Runaway on grade - brake testing, retarder use, escape lanes/berms
Edge of dump - windrows >= half wheel height, wheel stops at hopper
Tyre fires/explosions - 300 m exclusion for heated tyres (OEM guidance), tyre handler only
Fatigue - fatigue monitoring systems, shift design
Dust - water carts, cab pressurisation
sources: Caterpillar Performance Handbook (777 class); Komatsu HD785 specification
Thompson R.J. (2011/2015) Mine haul road design, construction & maintenance management (Univ. Pretoria / course notes)
EMESRT Design Philosophies; ISO 3471 (ROPS), ISO 3449 (FOPS), ISO 3450 (braking)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Maintain haul roads (graders/water carts) - rolling resistance strongly affects cycle time and tyre life
FMS ore-source assignment is the first stage of blending

equipment.name: Haul-road support: motor graders and water carts
equipment.function: Maintain haul road profile, crossfall and windrows (graders); suppress haul-road dust (water carts).
equipment.type_selected: ~16-ft blade motor grader (CAT 16M class, ~4.9 m blade); ~70-76 kL water cart on 90-t truck chassis (CAT 777 class) with spray bars and water cannon
key_dimensions: Grader length ~11 m, blade 4.9 m (OEM class)
Water cart tank ~70-76 kL on 777-class chassis (OEM class)
equipment.working_principle: The grader's mouldboard is set at an angle to cut ruts and potholes and windrow loose material, restoring the crown/crossfall that drains water off the road. The water cart's engine-driven centrifugal pump discharges through rear spray heads (controlled by the operator per head) and a front monitor cannon used also for fire fighting. Water binds fines so that wheel traffic does not raise dust; over-watering causes slippery roads, so intermittent application is used.
details_to_model: Grader: articulated frame, front tandem rear axles, mouldboard with circle and drawbar, rear ripper, cab with ROPS
Water cart: cylindrical/elliptical tank with baffles, top fill hatch with ladder and handrails, rear spray bar with 4-6 heads, front water cannon, side hose reel, pump housing
hazards_and_safety: Slippery roads from over-watering - intermittent sprays, never water ramps/intersections heavily
Grader on active haul road - radio calls, beacons
sources: Thompson R.J. haul road design notes

equipment.name: Mine support fleet (explosives MMU, fuel/lube truck, service truck, tyre handler, low loader, crane, emergency vehicles, light vehicles)
equipment.function: Charge blast holes, refuel and lubricate equipment in the field, change tyres, relocate tracked machines between pits, emergency response.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 MMU (contractor), 1 fuel/lube truck, 2 field service trucks, 1 tyre handler, 1 low loader (~100 t), 1 mobile crane (~60-100 t), 1 fire/rescue tender, 1 ambulance, ~20-30 light vehicles
equipment.type_selected: Purpose-built mining support vehicles (engineering estimate of fleet)
key_dimensions: Low loader: prime mover + ~100 t float, ~25-30 m long (engineering estimate)
Fuel truck: ~20-30 kL tank with hose reels and lube modules (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Support vehicles keep the production fleet in the field: the mobile manufacturing unit (MMU) mixes ammonium nitrate emulsion with sensitisers at the hole and pumps it down a hose; fuel/lube trucks use fast-fill dry-break couplings; the tyre handler grips and rotates the ~3-t tyres; low loaders move dozers/excavators between pits.
details_to_model: Light vehicles with buggy whip flags (orange flag + LED, ~4-5 m) and beacons
MMU with product bins and hose reel, explosives placards
Fuel truck with hose reels, fast-fill nozzle, spill kit
hazards_and_safety: Light vehicle - heavy vehicle interaction (highest fatality risk) - segregation, CAS
Explosives transport and handling - licensed, placarded
Tyre handling - tyre-handler only, exclusion zones

equipment.name: ROM pad with grade-bin stockpiles
equipment.function: Buffer between mining and sizing; holds ore in grade bins (e.g. high/low reactive silica, high/low available alumina) for controlled blending by wheel loader into the dump hopper when trucks are not direct-tipping.
equipment.type_selected: Compacted laterite pad with 4-6 finger stockpiles adjacent to the dump hopper ramp
key_dimensions: Pad area ~4-6 ha (engineering estimate)
Finger piles ~10-30 kt each, ~6-8 m high, end-tipped and dozer-trimmed (engineering estimate)
Total ROM buffer ~50-100 kt (~1-2 days mining) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Trucks either tip directly into the hopper or end-tip on a designated finger according to the FMS-assigned grade bin. Each finger has a sign board with its bin code and running grade. The loader blends from fingers in a ratio set by the mine geologist so that the sizer feed meets the reactive silica and available alumina targets.
details_to_model: Finger piles with coloured grade-bin signboards on posts
Bunded perimeter, drains to sediment pond
Lighting towers (mobile, 4 x LED) for night work
Windrows along tipping edges
hazards_and_safety: Truck tipping at pile edge - windrows, spotters avoided (use tip-and-push)
Loader-truck interaction - traffic management plan, one-way loop

equipment.name: Truck dump station (2-sided dump hopper) with pedestal rock breaker
equipment.function: Receives ROM ore from 90-t trucks and presents it to the apron feeder; rock breaker clears oversize/bridged boulders.
equipment.type_selected: Reinforced-concrete dump pocket with mechanically stabilised earth (MSE) or RC retaining walls and ramp; steel-lined hopper; hydraulic pedestal boom rock breaker
equipment.why_this_type: Two-sided tipping halves truck queueing; relocatable (semi-mobile) steel module option allows the station to be moved as mining fronts migrate (typical for dispersed plateau bauxite).
equipment.alternatives: Fully mobile in-pit sizer (track-mounted) for very dispersed pods; semi-mobile modular station (recommended for 10+ year moves).
key_dimensions: Hopper live capacity ~200-300 t (2-3 truck loads) (engineering estimate)
Hopper top opening ~12 m long x 8-9 m wide; tipping-deck height above apron feeder ~8-10 m (engineering estimate)
Wheel stop (concrete kerb/bumper block) ~1.2-1.4 m high (>= ~half tyre diameter of 2.7 m tyres) (engineering estimate per OEM guidance)
Rock breaker boom reach ~8-10 m, hammer ~1.5-2.5 t class (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: 400-500 HB abrasion-resistant steel, 25-40 mm (or rock-box ledges)

equipment.working_principle: Trucks reverse to the wheel stop and raise the body; the load slides into the hopper whose sloping walls (>= ~50-60 deg) direct ore onto the apron feeder. areas.area_name: Ore transport (mine to refinery overland conveyor system)
areas.purpose: Transport ~6.0-6.3 Mt/yr of sized wet bauxite from the mine sizing station to the refinery stockyard over a generic ~20 km route (plateau to valley, net fall ~150 m assumed) reliably, with low operating cost, minimal dust and low land impact.
areas.process_description: SELECTION - overland belt conveyor vs rail for 10-50 km: (a) Conveyor: continuous, electrically driven (low opex, can regenerate on downhill routes), low labour (remote-operated from refinery CCR), follows terrain with horizontal curves and grades up to ~15-18% (rail ~1-2%), single loading/discharge points match a single mine and single refinery, proven at this scale (e.g. ~51 km overland from Boddington mine to Worsley refinery, Western Australia; ~14.6 km single-flight cable-belt conveyor Panchpatmali mine to Damanjodi refinery, India - values to verify; Channar 20 km iron-ore overland, Nordell 1991). (b) Rail: favoured for >~50-100 km, multiple sources/customers, or existing rail; needs loop/loadout and car dumper, rolling stock, crews, flat gradients (heavy earthworks on plateau escarpments). (c) Slurry pipeline (e.g. Paragominas-Alunorte ~244 km) - only for very long distances; requires wet grinding at mine. DECISION: overland belt conveyor, 2 flights of ~10 km each (an intermediate transfer allows lower belt rating, and splits risk), fed by a relocatable field conveyor (~2-5 km) from the semi-mobile sizer. Sequence: sized ore from 01-CV-001 -> 02-CV-001 field conveyor -> 02-CV-002 overland flight 1 -> intermediate transfer station 02-TS-001 -> 02-CV-003 overland flight 2 -> refinery stockyard incoming conveyor 03-CV-001. Downhill sections are regenerative: drives with active-front-end VFDs return power to the grid and controlled caliper disc brakes ensure safe stopping. A full dynamic (transient) analysis governs starting/stopping ramps, take-up travel and brake sizing.

equipment.working_principle: An endless rubber belt with embedded longitudinal steel cords runs over pulleys at the ends and is supported by thousands of idler rolls in between. Drive pulleys at the head (and tail) transmit torque by friction (Euler-Eytelwein: T1/T2 <= e^(mu*theta)) from motors through gearboxes; a winch or gravity take-up keeps enough slack-side tension so the belt does not slip on the pulley and does not sag excessively between idlers. Over long distances the main resistance is indentation of the belt's bottom cover rolling over idlers, so a low-rolling-resistance cover compound substantially reduces power. Where the route descends, the load pulls the belt and the drives act as generators (regeneration), and controlled caliper brakes provide safe stopping. Starting and stopping are ramped by VFDs so that stress waves travelling along the elastic belt do not cause slip, belt lift-off in concave curves or excessive tension. Horizontal curves are achieved by tilting (banking) the idlers and by keeping belt tension within a band so the belt stays centred.

areas.layout_notes: Route ~20 km on a cleared corridor ~20-40 m wide containing the conveyor, a gravel patrol/maintenance road (one side), 33 kV overhead powerline and fibre-optic cable. Conveyor belt line ~1-1.5 m above ground on sleepers, rising onto trusses over roads/creeks; horizontal curves (R ~2-4 km) to follow ridgelines and avoid sensitive areas; vertical alignment follows terrain with concave/convex curve radii set by dynamic analysis (concave R typically several hundred to >1,000 m). Flight 1 tail at mine (drive station + loading chute from field conveyor), intermediate transfer station at ~10 km with drives, Flight 2 head at the refinery stockyard junction tower. Fauna crossings and stock crossings every ~1-2 km where required; dust/rain hoods throughout.

A03: delivers to 03-CV-001 (stockyard incoming conveyor) at the junction tower

Control: fibre-optic link; controlled from refinery central control room (CCR) and mine control room
Maintenance: shared heavy workshop / stores at refinery

areas.area_name: Bauxite receiving, stockpiling, blending and secondary crushing at the refinery
areas.purpose: Receive overland ore at up to 1,800 t/h, homogenise its quality in chevron blending beds to stabilise available alumina and reactive silica fed to digestion, provide strategic storage (monsoon/mine outage), sample and analyse the feed, remove tramp metal, reduce ore to mill-feed size (-40 mm nominal, subject to A04 mill selection) and fill the grinding mill feed bins at ~720 t/h wet average.
areas.process_description: 1) Ore arrives on 03-CV-001 at the junction tower; an on-line PGNAA analyser and belt scale record tonnage and elemental composition (Al2O3, SiO2, Fe2O3, TiO2) plus microwave moisture. 2) The yard conveyor with travelling tripper feeds a rail-mounted side-boom stacker that builds two in-line blending beds (A and B) by CHEVRON stacking: the stacker travels the full bed length at constant speed, laying ~300-500 thin layers on top of one another, so each cross-section contains material from the whole build period. 3) While one bed is being built, the other is reclaimed full-face by a bridge-type bucket-wheel reclaimer whose harrow rakes the whole cross-section; this cuts all layers simultaneously, giving variance reduction (blending effect) typically ~5-10:1 for chevron beds with this layer count. 4) A strategic/emergency stockpile (dozer-pushed, FEL-reclaimed through a ground hopper and vibrating feeder) holds 2-3 weeks of feed for mine/conveyor outages and monsoon disruptions. 5) Reclaimed ore passes an overband magnet, a metal detector and a mechanical cross-belt sampler (refinery feed sample for metallurgical accounting per ISO 8685). 6) Secondary sizing: 2 x 100% twin-shaft secondary sizers (one operating, one standby) reduce -200 mm ore to -40 mm nominal (P80 ~20-25 mm) for rod/ball-mill grinding; if A04 selects SAG mills, secondary sizing is reduced to a scalp/oversize breaker. 7) A shuttle/tripper conveyor distributes crushed ore to 3 mass-flow mill feed bins; weigh feeders under each bin meter ore into the grinding mills (A04), where lime and spent liquor are added. 8) Dust control: water sprays/fog at transfers, fog cannons on stockpiles, pulse-jet baghouse on the crusher house and bin tops. Stockyard runoff drains to a lined settlement pond and is recycled. No caustic is handled in A03 (first caustic contact is in A04 grinding).

equipment.name: Rail-mounted luffing side-boom stacker (chevron stacking)
equipment.function: Builds two in-line chevron blending beds and the emergency stockpile.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (emergency stockpile can also be fed by bypass chute/dozer if stacker is down)
equipment.type_selected: Travelling side stacker with luffing (non-slewing or limited-slew) boom fed by integral tripper
equipment.why_this_type: Chevron stacking along the bed centreline with a boom from the side of the yard is the standard linear blending bed arrangement; luffing keeps drop height low (dust, segregation).
equipment.alternatives: Circular blending store with slewing stacker and bridge scraper/bucket-wheel reclaimer (compact footprint, covered); slewing/luffing stacker-reclaimer (no blending).
key_dimensions: Boom length ~28-35 m (reaches bed centreline ~25 m from rail) (engineering estimate)
Rail gauge ~6-8 m; travel ~500-600 m (engineering estimate)
Machine mass ~200-350 t (engineering estimate)
Luffing range ~-12 to +18 deg; discharge height up to ~19-20 m

operating_parameters.basis: Calculated: ~110 kt bed / (~250-400 t per pass)

equipment.working_principle: The stacker travels continuously back and forth along the bed while discharging at the bed centreline; each pass lays a thin roof-shaped (chevron) layer. Over a few days, hundreds of layers accumulate, each representing a short period of mine production. Because the reclaimer later cuts across all layers at once, short-term quality fluctuations are averaged. A boom-tip level sensor lowers or raises (luffs) the boom to keep a small, constant drop height, minimising dust and size segregation. End-of-bed reversal is automatic, controlled by position encoders.

Integrated tripper car coupled to stacker

equipment.name: Bridge-type bucket-wheel blending reclaimer (full-face)
equipment.function: Reclaims the blending bed across its full cross-section to deliver blended ore at a controlled rate.
equipment.type_selected: Bridge reclaimer spanning the bed with traversing bucket wheel (or drum) and oscillating harrow
equipment.why_this_type: Full-face reclaiming is required to realise chevron blending; bucket-wheel/drum types handle sticky ore better than scrapers and allow high capacity.
equipment.alternatives: Drum reclaimer (full-width drum with buckets); bridge scraper reclaimer (lower capacity, more wear with abrasive ore).
key_dimensions: Bridge span (rail centres) ~52-55 m (engineering estimate)

Machine mass ~400-600 t (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The bridge advances slowly into the pile face. The harrow, a rake shaped like the pile cross-section, oscillates across the face and loosens a thin slice from all layers, which slides down to the toe. The bucket wheel, travelling to and fro along the bridge at the bottom of the face, scoops this material and discharges it onto the bridge conveyor, which feeds the yard reclaim conveyor 03-CV-002 through a chute. Reclaim rate is controlled by the bridge advance and wheel traverse speed, based on wheel motor power and downstream belt scale.

equipment.type_selected: Multistage centrifugal spray pump skid with filtration; tower- or mast-mounted fog cannons (oscillating, ~50-80 m throw); submersible sump pumps; lined settlement pond
key_dimensions: Fog cannon ~2-3 m long barrel on ~8-12 m mast (engineering estimate)
Settlement pond ~1-2 ha, 3 m deep, HDPE-lined (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (avoid wet ore stickiness and water into refinery balance)

equipment.working_principle: Fine water droplets either wet the ore (sprays at transfers) or agglomerate airborne particles so they fall out (fog cannons). Sprays are interlocked to run only when material is flowing. Stockyard runoff carries fines to the pond, where they settle; clear water is pumped back to the spray system or process water.
details_to_model: Spray bars with flat-fan nozzles at each transfer chute, solenoid valves
Fog cannons on masts with fan housing and nozzle ring
Pump skid in small shed, filters, pressure gauges
Concrete-lined drains and sumps around beds, pond with access ramp for cleanout, fencing and life rings
hazards_and_safety: Slippery surfaces; electrical in wet areas; drowning in pond

areas.layout_notes: Stockyard on the refinery's up-wind side (relative to prevailing wind towards offices) at grade, adjacent to the grinding area (A04). Junction tower where the overland enters, then an in-line yard ~500-550 m long x ~110-130 m wide: incoming conveyor and stacker rails on one side, two beds (each ~50 m wide, ~200-220 m overall) end to end, bridge reclaimer rails straddling the beds (~52-55 m span), reclaim conveyor on the opposite side, emergency stockpile (~250-350 kt; ~250 x 120 m footprint, ~15-18 m high) beside the yard with its ground hopper. Inclined covered gallery (~12-15 deg) from the yard to the crusher house (~30-35 m high), then a second gallery up to the mill-feed bin building located directly above/beside the grinding mills so bins discharge by gravity via weigh feeders into the mill feed chutes. Ground-level perimeter access road (~6 m) around yard for maintenance, fire access and loader cleanup. Electrical substation and MCC rooms near the crusher house; settlement pond at the low corner of the yard.
interfaces: A02: receives up to 1,800 t/h from 02-CV-003
A04 Grinding/milling: crushed ore at ~720 t/h wet via weigh feeders to each mill; lime and liquor added in A04; mill type sets crushed top size
Laboratory/QA: sample increments, analyser data, refinery feed reconciliation with mine (A01) FMS tonnages
Utilities: process/raw water for dust suppression, compressed air for bag house/air cannons, power
Control: CCR (stockyard machines automatic mode, interlocked conveyor sequences)

open_questions: IMPORTANT: live web search/fetch was blocked in this run, so no online verification was possible. Sources are cited from established literature and standards; items marked 'verify' (Worsley ~51 km conveyor, NALCO ~14.6 km cable-belt at ~1,800 t/h, vendor class data) and all 'engineering estimate' values should be checked by the SME review / a follow-up research pass.

A04 grinding mill type (rod/ball vs SAG) decides whether secondary sizing to -40 mm is needed and the mill-feed top size; also confirm the number of grinding lines (3 assumed) and therefore the number of mill feed bins.

Site terrain for the generic route: assumed ~20 km with ~150 m net fall (plateau to valley). A net-uphill or flat route changes drive location, brake requirements and power; confirm before 3-D modelling of drive stations.
Bauxite factor changed to ~2.7 t/t (from 2.4-2.6); the digestion/mass-balance author should confirm with their available alumina definition and recovery assumptions.
Is the hard caprock treated as ore (Darling Range practice) or waste (common for some Indian laterite cappings)? This changes strip ratio and drill & blast quantities.
Monsoon climate: decide whether blending beds are roofed (long portal sheds) - significant visual/modelling impact - and confirm emergency stockpile size (15-20 days assumed).
Truck class: 90-t class selected for selectivity and dispersed pits; owner may prefer 136-t class (fewer trucks, wider roads) or electrified/autonomous fleet - confirm for modelling.
Primary sizing station: semi-mobile (relocatable modules) assumed; confirm relocation interval and whether a fully mobile in-pit sizer is preferred.
Use of PGNAA on-line analyser (radioactive source licensing) vs laboratory-only quality control - owner preference.
Grade-control spec limits (reactive SiO2 ceiling, available Al2O3 floor, blending variance targets) to be set jointly with the refinery process team.
